title: Serial-Port Terminal — Overview and definition
description: Opens UART/USB-serial consoles to talk to firmware, bootloaders, and instruments.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Opens UART/USB-serial consoles to talk to firmware, bootloaders, and instruments. A serial-port terminal opens COM/tty devices at configurable baud rates, sends and receives text and binary frames, and logs sessions with timestamps. Real implementations include PuTTY, Tera Term, minicom, screen, and the Arduino serial monitor. It handles flow control (RTS/CTS, XON/XOFF), line-ending translation, and macro buttons for common commands.
capabilities: Open serial ports at standard and custom baud rates with full parity/stop-bit control
Send text lines, hex bytes, and scripted command sequences
Log sessions with timestamps for later analysis
Plot incoming numeric streams as scrolling charts
Trigger DTR/RTS for bootloader entry and board reset

title: Serial-Port Terminal — Actual implementation
description: Opens UART/USB-serial consoles to talk to firmware, bootloaders, and instruments.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. How Serial-Port Terminal is actually implemented. A serial-port terminal opens COM/tty devices at configurable baud rates, sends and receives text and binary frames, and logs sessions with timestamps. Real implementations combine GUI terminal, CLI (minicom/screen), scripting API with OS serial drivers, USB-CDC/FTDI drivers for adapters. The implementation is verified by Verify with a loopback plug: transmitted bytes return unaltered at 115200 8N1, and a 1 MB transfer shows zero framing errors

title: Serial-Port Terminal — Teaching-ladder exercise
description: Opens UART/USB-serial consoles to talk to firmware, bootloaders, and instruments.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Teaching ladder for Serial-Port Terminal, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Open serial ports at standard and custom baud rates with full parity/stop-bit control). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Open serial ports at standard and custom baud rates with full parity/stop-bit control and Send text lines, hex bytes, and scripted command sequences. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (Microcontroller programming environment) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
